```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"DSA notes with dismay that current discussions and hearings in Congress relating to national health insurance have excluded single-payer health insurance from the discussion.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The plans under discussion presume a large role for the existing insurance industry, possibly in competition with a Medicare-like public option.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA strongly supports single payer over other alternatives.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA feels it is vitally important to include supporters of single payer in the discussion around all possible plans.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA condemns the exclusion of single-payer supporters in both President Obama’s Health Care Summit and in the hearings of the Senate Finance Committee.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The ideas and experience of health-care professionals committed to the single-payer approach would provide essential input in discussions of public options.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The current political situation provides the best opportunity for serious health-care reform in a generation.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"DSA does not accept the position that unless they get everything they want, they are willing to see the opportunity for health-care reform disappear.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"DSA believes the insurance industry is powerful enough that the current political dynamic could result in a “health care reform” that is worse than nothing at all, because it would create a public plan that is designed to fail.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
